reuse.why: Extends the existing exported getScheduledAmount helper and the existing getApproxNumberThreshold rule helper rather than writing new amount logic.

duplication.why: All five inline midpoint copies (updateActions, postTransactionForSchedule, computeSchedulePreviewTransactions, forecast normalizeSchedule, schedule-template) are removed and routed through the one helper; the API field reuses it too.

placement.why: The rule lives in shared/schedules.ts, where the helper already lived and which both server and client import; the API only adds a field in its handler and type.

scope.why: Focused on the amount rule and the API field, with tests and a release note; the client call sites are touched only to pass the operator.

maintainability.why: One small function now owns the whole expected-amount rule; the positional (amount, op, inverse) signature forces a null placeholder when only inverse is needed, and passing the op in useScheduleEdit's op-switch conversion is a subtle coupling.

bypasses_abstraction.where: Every caller goes through getScheduledAmount from #shared/schedules.

disguised_duplication.where: No reshaped copies remain; the inline ternaries were deleted, not renamed.

abstraction_drift.where: getScheduledAmount gains one amountOp parameter that carries the rule's real variation (approximate amounts); the isapprox branch is part of the rule itself, not a caller-specific special case; no call site bypasses it.
